note: A run aimed at the 3rd of the arriving chord over a ii–V–I backing track: from below, then from above, then a run of the singer's own aimed at the 3rd or the 7th. The staff's line rings the note to hold and the note to land on over each chord, and the chords are tokens counted the long way. The old copy in C is now moves (any key, 72 to 96 bpm), so the second block changes the task, not the key, and the line about another key is marked {{?key}}.

exercise.title: A run into the chord
exercise.why: A run sounds placed, not just decorative, when its last note belongs to the chord that is arriving, so aim every run at the 3rd of the next chord.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. The backing track plays {{chord:ii7}}, {{chord:V7}}, then two bars of {{chord:Imaj7}}.
{{chord:ii7}} is the 2nd chord of the key, built on {{2}}, {{chord:V7}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}, and {{chord:Imaj7}} is the 1st chord, built on {{1}}. Hold the ringed {{4}} through {{chord:ii7}} and {{chord:V7}}. At the end of the {{chord:V7}} bar, sing the run {{1}}, {{2}}, {{3}} and land on {{3}} as {{chord:Imaj7}} arrives. Sing the long note on "oo" and the run on "ah".
Practice until {{3}} lands on the first beat of {{chord:Imaj7}} every time round.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together. Hold {{4}} as before, and at the end of the {{chord:V7}} bar sing the run {{5}}, {{4}}, {{3}} into the same {{3}}. Sing it on "ah".
If the run lands late, start it half a beat earlier, not faster.
{{?key}}In another key the chords are new, but the run still ends on {{3}} on the first beat of the 1st chord.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together. Make up a run of your own from the whole scale each time round, and aim it at a ringed note, {{3}} or {{7}}, as {{chord:Imaj7}} arrives. Sing it on any vowel you like.
Then leave the next bar empty before the next run.
